name: Maharashtra

sub_regions.name: Mumbai and Thane
sub_regions.notes: Metropolitan region; Koliwadas, East Indian gaothans, every community of the state and migrants from across India.

sub_regions.name: Konkan coast
sub_regions.notes: Palghar, Raigad, Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg: coast, paddy and coconut; Warli areas in Palghar.

sub_regions.name: Western Maharashtra (Desh)
sub_regions.notes: Pune, Satara, Sangli, Kolhapur, Solapur: sugarcane belt, Sahyadri hills, Pandharpur.

sub_regions.name: North Maharashtra and Khandesh
sub_regions.notes: Nashik, Jalgaon, Dhule, Nandurbar, Ahilyanagar: vineyards, onion and banana farms, tribal belt in the north-west.

sub_regions.name: Marathwada
sub_regions.notes: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Paithan, Latur, Nanded and nearby: dry farmland; Paithani weaving.

sub_regions.name: Vidarbha
sub_regions.notes: Nagpur, Amravati, Gadchiroli and nearby: cotton and oranges, forests in the east; Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur.

communities.name: Hindu
communities.notes: Men: shirt and trousers daily; dhoti, kurta and bandi among older rural men; kurta with a pheta for festivals. Women: cotton saree or salwar-kameez daily; nauvari or Paithani for festivals; mangalsutra and green bangles when married.

communities.name: Koli (fisherfolk)
communities.notes: Original fishing community of Mumbai's Koliwadas. Women: brightly coloured lugra saree with a white khadki scarf, hair in a bun with flowers. Men: red Koli cap, festive surka waist-cloth. Narali Purnima.

communities.name: Buddhist (Ambedkarite)
communities.notes: Followers of Dr B. R. Ambedkar's Navayana Buddhism; Dhammachakra Pravartan Din at Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur. Dress follows everyday Maharashtrian dress; no specific dress sourced yet.

communities.name: Muslim
communities.notes: Dakhni-Urdu speaking Muslims across the state (large communities in Mumbai, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Malegaon), Konkani Muslims on the coast. Specific dress not yet sourced; characters wear shared kurta-pyjama and salwar-kameez.

communities.name: Jain
communities.notes: Mostly urban trading families; everyday Maharashtrian and modern dress. Monastic robes not depicted.

communities.name: East Indian Catholic
communities.notes: Mumbai's oldest Catholic community (Vasai, Uttan, Manori-Gorai and Mumbai gaothans). Women wear the lugra, a nine-yard saree with its own drape (green lugra at Agera); harvest feast Agera in October.

communities.name: Warli (Adivasi)
communities.notes: Adivasi community of Palghar and Thane districts. Women: four-yard lugda sari with choli; married women wear a black-bead kali ganthi necklace. Men: half-sleeved shirt or sleeveless jacket with shorts. Festivals incl. Holi and Diwali.

communities.name: Parsi
communities.notes: Small Zoroastrian community, mostly in Mumbai. No characters yet; sudreh and kusti are sacred garments and are not depicted.

look_range.hair: Black hair, straight or wavy; older women in a bun (khopa or ambada).
look_range.notes: Wheatish to deep brown; deeper tones common among coastal and rural working communities. Starting range, tune after test renders.

naming.notes: Marathi custom: given name plus father's name (e.g. Sneha Prakash). Most Marathi surnames mark caste or clan; never use them.
Arabic or Persian-origin given name plus father's name.
Christian given names with Portuguese-origin surnames (not caste names).

heritage.name: Maratha and Peshwa court dress
heritage.reason: Historical court dress waits for the era phase; real historical rulers are never depicted.

heritage.name: Shivaji Maharaj costumes, swords and portrait flags at Shiv Jayanti
heritage.reason: The festival is shown through lezim, dhol and festive dress; nobody is dressed as a real historical figure, no weapons are shown, and flags are plain (no portraits).

heritage.name: Dhol-tasha pathaks
heritage.reason: Played in Maratha battles and celebrations, tied to Ganeshotsav since the 19th century; shown as processions. Player uniform waits for a real source.

heritage.name: Puneri pagadi
heritage.reason: GI-protected symbol of honour worn on special occasions; kept as a restricted honour item and never auto-selected. The everyday festive pheta is used instead.

heritage.name: Warkari tulsi mala and forehead marks
heritage.reason: The tulsi mala and gopichandan marks belong to practising Warkaris; characters may appear at the Wari only as pilgrims in ordinary dress.

heritage.name: Mardani khel and weapons
heritage.reason: Weapons are excluded from the public library.

avoid: Caste labels or caste surnames (e.g. Patil, Deshmukh, Kulkarni); caste or reservation politics.
Real historical figures (e.g. Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Peshwas) or lookalikes.
Lavani dance costume or any glamour framing of Maharashtrian women.
Mumbai slum, poverty or 'Bollywood' cliches; farmer distress or drought framing.
Communal or political imagery (party flags, riots, language politics).
Warkari tulsi mala or forehead marks on characters; Jain monastic robes; Parsi sacred garments.
Nauvari shown only as a costume: it is also everyday dress for many older rural women.
Anyone dressed as Shivaji Maharaj, swords or sticks, or flags with a real person's portrait (Shiv Jayanti is shown through lezim, dhol and festive dress).
